In [[cryptography]], '''Spectr-H64''' is a [[block cipher]] designed in 2001 by N. D. Goots, A. A. Moldovyan and N. A. Moldovyan. It relies heavily on the [[permutation]] of individual bits, so  is much better suited to implementation in hardware than in software.

The algorithm has a [[block size (cryptography)|block size]] of 64 bits and [[key size]] of 256 bits. It uses a 12-round structure in which half of the block determines the transformation of the other half in each round, similar to a [[Feistel cipher]] or [[RC5]]. This same basic design was repeated in its successor, [[CIKS-1]].

==Cryptanalysis==

An analysis of Spectr-H64 was presented in 2002 by Selçuk Kavut and Melek D Yücel of the Middle East Technical University, showing a method of using a [[differential attack]] to retrieve half of the key bits when a single round is used. Using this method, they then presented a [[slide attack]] that requires 2<sup>17</sup> chosen plaintexts to return all key bits on the full 12 rounds.
